title: Choose the visual world for ContentPulse
question: The roll assigned the Contact Sheet. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. It will cover the new landing page and the whole app.

options.label: The Contact Sheet
options.lineage: a photo editor's contact sheet, marked up in china marker
options.thesis: Every trend is a frame on the sheet; the client's fit is the grease-pencil circle around the selects.
options.viewport: Landing: today's trends printed as a 36-frame contact sheet with edge numbers; red circles land on the three frames that fit an example agency client, a loupe lifts one select into its finished LinkedIn post, and Start free sits in the sheet's margin.
options.risk: Could read as a photography tool if frames show pictures; every frame must carry a headline, a score and a source.

raised.raise: Every frame's fit score is measured on one visible 0-100 scale printed along the film edge, never eyeballed.
All neutrals come from one fixed tonal ramp of paper-to-film steps; no stray greys anywhere in the app.
Every status is a named mark (circle, cross, star, OK stamp) with a word, never colour alone.
Each trend frame leads with the post it could become, and turns over to show its sources.

options.label: The Wire Desk
options.lineage: a newsroom wire desk: teleprinter copy, slug lines and priority flags
options.thesis: Trends arrive as wire copy; the desk spikes what doesn't fit and runs what does.
options.viewport: Landing: a live wire scrolling down the left with URGENT slugs on items that fit the client; the chosen item is set in type as a finished post on the right, with Start free in the masthead.
options.risk: Newsroom looks are common for content tools; this is the familiar choice.

options.label: Signal Bench
options.lineage: a CRT oscilloscope on a signal bench
options.thesis: Trends as signals; the relevance threshold is the trigger level.
options.viewport: A phosphor trace with the client's trigger level locking relevant signals still.
options.case: Fuses poorly: agency marketers don't recognise a lab bench, and signal-versus-noise needs explaining.
options.kept: One measured scale for every score.
options.risk: Reads as an engineering tool to a marketing audience.

options.label: Exposure Record
options.lineage: a darkroom printer's exposure record with zone sheets
options.thesis: Overlapping sheets where hatch density shows load and conflict.
options.viewport: Translucent sheets over a backlit zone ramp, hatched by score.
options.case: Fuses poorly: hatching and stop-deltas hide the simple trend-to-post story.
options.kept: A strict tonal ramp as the only neutrals.
options.risk: Too abstract for a first-time visitor.

options.label: Cyclorama Dawn
options.lineage: theatre lighting on a cyclorama, night to day
options.thesis: A trend's life as light rising from night to day.
options.viewport: A horizon band rising from black as a trend gains fit.
options.case: Fuses poorly: atmosphere carries the mood, not the workflow.
options.kept: Named states that never rely on colour alone.
options.risk: Beautiful but vague about what the product does.

options.label: Seed Packet Rack
options.thesis: Each item shows its promise on the front and instructions on the back.
options.viewport: A rack of trend packets ranked by season, each flipping to its plan.
options.case: Fuses poorly: agencies don't identify with gardening, though promise-then-instructions fits.
options.kept: Lead with the post each trend could become.

options.label: Akari Workshop
options.lineage: washi paper lamps over bamboo ribs
options.thesis: Active items glow; dismissed ones fold flat.
options.viewport: Glowing paper volumes for the trends that fit.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no link to agency work or to trends.
options.kept: A clear lit versus folded-away state.

options.label: Chaekgeori Shelves
options.thesis: Shelves that open toward the viewer as you go deeper.
options.viewport: A cabinet of trend boxes widening toward you.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the spatial trick obscures the task.
options.risk: Hard to read at a glance.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A modern SaaS landing page and app, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Headline, sub-copy, sign-up button and a product screenshot, then feature sections.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other content tools by design.
